description: Master manifest for medical corpus generation. Every row tells the scraper: go to this source and fetch the page for this medical topic. The scraper reads this manifest and remains completely generic — all search behavior lives here. This manifest also serves as a medical knowledge graph specification, mapping topics to blood tests, clinical domains, related conditions, and patient questions.

summary_generation.description: After all sources are scraped for a topic, generate a merged summary.md that synthesizes the best information from all sources. This becomes the Layer 2 canonical knowledge document and the primary retrieval target for RAG.

layers.layer_1_raw: Raw scraped documents. Never modify. Ground truth.
layers.layer_2_canonical: summary.md — generated from all sources. Primary retrieval document.
layers.layer_3_vectors: Chunked and embedded from Layer 2. Stored in vector database.

document_id_scheme.description: Stable identifier for every scraped article. Each chunk in the vector database carries this ID plus chunk index for full traceability.

ada.name: American Diabetes Association
ada.notes: Primary authority for diabetes-specific clinical guidelines and patient education.

niddk.name: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases
niddk.notes: NIH institute — authoritative on diabetes, kidney, liver, and digestive diseases.

mayo.name: Mayo Clinic
mayo.notes: Comprehensive patient-facing medical encyclopedia. Excellent for tests, procedures, and conditions.

medlineplus.name: MedlinePlus
medlineplus.notes: NLM consumer health resource. Strong coverage of lab tests, drugs, and conditions in plain language.

cleveland.name: Cleveland Clinic
cleveland.notes: Strong coverage of diagnostics, lab tests, and cardiovascular topics.

cdc.name: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
cdc.notes: Public health authority. Strong on prevention, epidemiology, and lifestyle guidance.

Status stages: pending → scraped → cleaned → chunked → embedded → verified → ready.
Each topic folder contains one .md file per source (e.g., ada_v1.md, mayo_v1.md, niddk_v1.md).
Each topic folder also contains metadata.json tracking url, scraped_on, word_count, content_hash, and version.
After all sources are scraped, a summary.md (Layer 2) is generated from all sources for each topic.
The queries object maps source keys to site-specific search strings because each site titles pages differently.
The medications module is marked as 'future' — not for the current assignment but structurally ready.
Sources were selected for each topic based on which organization is the recognized authority for that domain.
related_tests maps topics to actual blood test parameter names as they appear in lab reports for direct report-to-knowledge lookup.
related_topics creates a knowledge graph enabling traversal from any concept to clinically related concepts.
clinical_tags enable fast filtering without embeddings — e.g., filter(tag=='kidney') returns all renal content.
patient_questions drive future QA pair generation and inform chatbot prompt engineering.
source_priority defines evidence hierarchy — if sources disagree, higher-ranked sources are trusted first.
reading_level starts at 'patient' and can later be expanded to 'medical_student' and 'doctor' for multi-audience content.
refresh_interval guides re-scraping schedule — fast-changing topics (GLP-1: 6 months) vs stable topics (anatomy: 5 years).
document_id (KB-XXXXXX) provides a stable identifier for traceability from vector database chunks back to source documents.
